sweep_summary: Catalan (stan1289) is in the catalog as 'lexical' on Mascaró 1976 (with GIEC 2016 downloaded earlier as co-deciding). Of the 11 title-hits, only three concern word stress: Faust & Torres-Tamarit 2017 (Glossa, open; downloaded via the Internet Archive copy of the HAL author PDF) gives a clean first-hand statement — regular stress = final in C-final nominals, penult in V-final ones, lexical stress anywhere in a right-edge three-syllable window, morphology mostly irrelevant — which confirms the catalog's classification; Torres-Tamarit & Pons-Moll 2015 (Going Romance talk, published 2019 in J. Linguistics, paywalled; abstract read) adds Balearic verb+enclitic stress shift and calls the unmarked nominal pattern a right-aligned moraic trochee (refines); Roca 1999 (Eurotyp Romance-stress survey, De Gruyter, paywalled, no open copy anywhere) is the one unread item worth acquiring (priority high). Cabré & Prieto 2004 (Probus; author copy downloaded from the archived UPF prosody site) is about glide formation but states Catalan's preference for trochaic feet and avoidance of antepenultimate stress (consistent). The rest are intonation/phrasing/syllabification work (Prieto & Rigau 2007 and Vanrell et al. 2014 downloaded and read, silent on word stress; Feldhausen 2008/2010, Vanrell 2013 and Torres-Tamarit & Pons-Moll 2012 judged from abstracts/titles, none read in full; Cabré & Prieto 2005 paywalled, low priority). No item contradicts the catalog; nothing read supersedes Mascaró 1976 as deciding source, but Faust & Torres-Tamarit 2017 should be added as an open, modern supporting citation. discovery used Unpaywall, Crossref, HAL and the Internet Archive's index APIs instead.

new_statements.quote: In Catalan, nominal forms have either regular or lexical stress. Regular stress falls on the last vowel if the word is consonant-final (11a) and on the penultimate vowel if the word is vowel-final (11b). [...] Lexical stress can appear on any vowel within a right-oriented three-syllable window. Penultimate stress is exceptional in consonant-final words (12a), final stress is exceptional in vowel-final words (12b), and there are also words ending in a vowel or a consonant that show antepenultimate stress (12c). [...] Morphological structure is in most cases irrelevant for stress assignment.

new_statements.reading: A concise modern statement by two native-speaker phonologists: Catalan nominal stress is lexically specified within a right-edge three-syllable window, with a strong statistical default of final stress in consonant-final words and penultimate stress in vowel-final words; verbs are set aside. This matches the catalog's 'lexical' coding (Mascaró 1976: any of the last three syllables, lexically determined, oxytones commonest, proparoxytones rarest) and the GIEC 2016 statement already. it also documents, in the field's own words, the 'regular vs lexical' framing that explains why StressTyp2 codes Catalan as quantity-sensitive (final-if-C-final else penult). It adds the note that the plural -s never attracts stress and that the same default extends to /n/-final stems after n-deletion.

new_statements.quote: En català, l'accent de mot és lliure i pot recaure en una de les tres últimes síl·labes, com apareix exemplificat en el quadre 5.1. [...] La posició de l'accent està condicionada en part per l'estructura fonològica, i especialment pel caràcter lliure (quan acaba en vocal) o travat (quan acaba en consonant) de l'última síl·laba. Notem en aquest sentit que la major part del lèxic està format per mots aguts acabats en consonant (prat, desert, francès, ric, Aleix, lluny, avall) i per mots plans acabats en vocal (mare, cadira, Pere, Aina, ara).
new_statements.translation: In Catalan, word stress is free and can fall on one of the last three syllables, as exemplified in table 5.1. [...] The position of stress is conditioned in part by phonological structure, and especially by the open (vowel-final) or closed (consonant-final) character of the last syllable. Note in this regard that most of the lexicon consists of oxytone words ending in a consonant (prat, desert, francès, ric, Aleix, lluny, avall) and paroxytone words ending in a vowel (mare, cadira, Pere, Aina, ara).

The catalog record for Catalan (qs-tier-2026-09-12) has an empty rule field; this is the authoritative source to fill it, and it adds verbs (morphological), suffix classes, compounds, and dialectal enclitic stress shift.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is free (lexically distinctive: tribu/tribú, sumis/sumís, pública/publica) within a right-edge three-syllable window; the strong tendency in non-verbal forms is stress on the last vowel of the stem, giving final stress in consonant-final words and penultimate stress in vowel-final (inflected) words, with rarer stem-final-vowel oxytones (cafè, menú), stem-penult paroxytones (àrab, examen) and very few antepenults (Júpiter, hàbitat). Verb forms are all paroxytone or oxytone with stress fixed by the morphology (root, theme vowel or tense marker); suffixes are stressed (-er, -al) or pre-stressing (-ic); in prefixed words and compounds the right-hand member keeps the stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: §1.3: within a prosodic group one distinguishes a primary stress and one or more secondary stresses of varying intensity; §5.2.2: in Valencian dialects clitics can take secondary stress in sequences like porta-li-la; §5.2.1.3: the left member of compounds loses its stress but not its vowel quality.
new_statements.exceptions: §5.2.1.1: learned/foreign words with unaccepted stress shifts (míssil, monòlit, alfil, olimpíades..) and a few accepted doublets (antílop/antilop, xòfer/xofer, saxofon/saxòfon); Northern (septentrional) dialect pronounces proparoxytones as paroxytones (practica for pràctica); Balearic and Northern colloquial elision of final -ia in esdrúixols. §5.2.2: in Mallorcan and Menorcan, verb + enclitic sequences take stress on the last syllable (comprar-mé, dur-hó), avoided in formal registers; Northern imperative + enclitic likewise final.
new_statements.identity_note: Mascaró 1976 uses the Catalan of Barcelona; Ortega-Llebaria & Prieto 2011 describe Central Catalan; Torres-Tamarit & Pons-Moll cover Barcelona, Formentera, Mallorca and Menorca Catalan (dialect-specific stress shift onto verb + enclitic sequences: none in Barcelona, penult/final in Formentera, final in Mallorca and Menorca); GIEC 2016 describes the standard with dialect notes (Mallorcan/Menorcan and Northern enclitic final stress, Northern flattening of proparoxytones, Valencian secondary stress on clitics).

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is within the final three syllables; the unmarked nominal pattern (about 86% of inflected word forms per Serra 1996) is penultimate in vowel-final words and final in consonant-final words, analysed as a right-aligned moraic trochee with weight-to-stress (heavy final syllable attracts stress); marked patterns (C-final paroxytones incl. pre-stressing suffixes -ic/-fil; V-final oxytones, mostly underlying /n/, /r/ or loans; antepenults, never with a closed penult except loans like Manchester) must be lexically specified. Verbal stress is morphologized (Oltra-Massuet). new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is underlying (lexically specified per morpheme) and limited to one of the last three vowels; oxytones commonest, proparoxytones rarest; major-category words are always stressed; in polymorphemic words the last stressed morpheme wins (Destressing rule (24)); affixes are unstressed, stressed (-al, -er, future/conditional markers, theme vowels) or pre-stressing (-ic); verb stems are oxytone and verbal stress follows from stressed theme vowels and tense markers. §§2-3 review and reject Wheeler's (1974) rule-based Major/Minor Stress Rules (C-final = final, V-final = penult) because of proparoxytones (vèrtebra, Júpiter, dèficit), V-final oxytones without underlying r (cafè, tabú, sofà) and future/conditional stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Compounds are treated as two-stress words (p. 26); no word-level secondary stress rule stated in the pages read.
new_statements.exceptions: Proparoxytones (vèrtebra, òmicron, íntegra, Hèlsinki, Júpiter, dèficit), polysyllables ending in a stressed vowel (mercè, ximpanzé, vostè, tarannà, tabú, sofà, cafè, peroné), future/conditional desinence stress, irregular caber/saber subjunctives (càpiga, sàpiga).

readall_conflicts: No source disagrees on the facts: every opened work places Catalan word stress within the last three syllables, non-predictable in general but with a strong C-final = final / V-final = penultimate default in nominals and morphologically fixed stress in verbs. The only divergence is analytic framing: Mascaró 1976 treats stress as underlying and memorized for each morpheme (rejecting Wheeler's rule-based account), while Torres-Tamarit & Pons-Moll 2018/2019, following Serra 1996 and Vallverdú 1997, derive the unmarked pattern from a weight-sensitive right-aligned moraic trochee that covers about 86% of inflected forms and treat the rest as lexical exceptions; GIEC 2016 calls the accent 'lliure' (free) while stating the same tendencies. This is why a quantity-sensitive coding (StressTyp2-style) and a lexical coding both have textual support; the sources themselves describe one system.

Regular stress falls on the last vowel if the word is consonant-final (11a) and on the penultimate vowel if the word is vowel-final (11b). [...] Lexical stress can appear on any vowel within a right-oriented three-syllable window. Penultimate stress is exceptional in consonant-final words (12a), final stress is exceptional in vowel-final words (12b), and there are also words ending in a vowel or a consonant that show antepenultimate stress (12c). [...] Morphological structure is in most cases irrelevant for stress assignment.
sources.locator: §2.2 'Stress in Catalan', Art. 63 pp.7-8 (the text), with tables (11)-(12) and algorithm (13); also §1 p.3 (the text)
sources.note: Nominal stress = regular default (C-final -> final: [əlməˈnak], [pəˈtit]; V-final -> penult: [nəˈɣɔsi], [munˈtaɲə]) plus lexical stress anywhere in a right-edge three-syllable window ([kəˈpitul], [təˈβu], [məˈtɾɔpuli]); plural -s does not attract stress; stress-attracting but unstressed suffixes (-ic); most prior accounts (Cabré 1993, Serra 1996, Vallverdú 1997, Bonet & Lloret 1998) use a right-aligned moraic trochee with a final-consonant mora, which the authors replace by an empty-nucleus account. Also: 'final stress in Catalan is most commonly found in consonant-final words'.
sources.venue: Glossa: a journal of general linguistics

sources.citation: Feldhausen, Ingo (2008). The prosody-syntax interface in Catalan. PhD dissertation, University of Potsdam.
sources.quote: [p.38] For Catalan, a language that has lexical stress, the basic idea is by and large clear; a stressed non-compound lexical word together with any adjacent clitic counts as a prosodic word. Elements in Catalan which cannot bear primary word stress are inter alia prepositions (which are [p.39] often also asyllabic), determiners, and (weak) pronouns. [...] Prosodic words in Catalan consist of at least a moraic trochee (Cabré 1993) and the primary word stress falls on the rightmost stressable element (Wheeler 2004:1). [...] [p.56] I chose proparoxytonic words (paraules esdrúixoles) in the target positions of my experiments. Their stress is located on the antepenultimate syllable
sources.locator: Ch. 2 'Fundamental Aspects of Catalan Intonation', sec. 2.1 'The Autosegmental-Metrical (AM) model', thesis pp. 38-39 (pp. 46-47); sec. 2.3.2 'The Continuation Rise', thesis p. 56 (p. 64); vowel reduction in sec. 1.1.1 'Central Catalan', pp. 4-6

sources.quote: The most superficial observation about Catalan stress is that words are either unstressed, or else stressed on one of the last three syllables. [...] Although oxytones are more common than paroxytones, and proparoxytones are least common, there is no clear correlation between place of stress or any other general property of morphemes. [p. 19] [...] (23) stress, rather than being a feature added in the course of the derivation, is like other segmental features part of the underlying representation of morphemes. [...] First, conditions on well-formedness of underlying representations will restrict it to one of the three last vowels, the rest remaining unstressed. [pp. 33-34]

sources.citation: Torres-Tamarit, Francesc and Pons-Moll, Clàudia (2015). Enclitic-triggered stress shift in Catalan. Paper delivered at Going Romance 29, Radboud University, Nijmegen. [Published as: Torres-Tamarit & Pons-Moll (2019). Enclitic-induced stress shift in Catalan. Journal of Linguistics 55(2): 407-444.]
sources.quote: In this paper we provide a novel and unified formal analysis of the stress microvariation found in verb–enclitic groupings in Barcelona Catalan, with stress stability, in Formentera Catalan, with stress shift to the penultimate and the last syllable of the whole sequence, and in Mallorca and Menorca Catalan, with stress shift to the last syllable. We argue that stress shift in Formentera Catalan conforms directly to the unmarked pattern of nominal stress in Catalan, that is, a right-aligned moraic trochee, with the constraint All-Feet-Right undominated, leading to final and penultimate stress.
sources.locator: Published abstract (Crossref metadata and Cambridge Core product page for 10.1017/S0022226718000427)
sources.note: Verb+enclitic stress: stable in Barcelona Catalan, shifts to penult/final (Formentera) or to the final syllable (Mallorca, Menorca); treats the unmarked nominal stress pattern as a right-aligned moraic trochee giving final (C-final) or penultimate (V-final) stress. Adds Balearic clitic-group stress shift, which the catalog record does not mention.

sources.quote: Distance of the vocoid sequence from the main word stress is another factor which conditions glide formation: the greater the distance, the greater the tendency to pronounce a diphthong. [...] Glide formation in this context can be easily explained by the strong prosodic preference for trochaic feet (and the avoidance of antepenultimate stress) shown by the Catalan language: històr[iə] > històr[jə] 'history'; àv[iə] > àv[jə] 'grandmother'.
